name: upgrade-reconciliation-final-review
body:
Reconciliation for the final implementation review of project upgrade. The review found four spec points where the implementation legitimately settled the behaviour; the durable spec is reconciled to the code, with unaffected text preserved. Two of the divergences were already flagged as observations during implementation (upgrade/plan.note-19: format-migration source-only keying; upgrade/plan.note-29: deck validated through the full `kalide start` pipeline).

1. domain.value.format-migration said each migration 'names its source and target version'. The code keys a migration only on its source format: `formatMigration` carries a single `sourceFormat` field and `migrationChain` walks current, current+1, …, target-1, so the target is always the next format (internal/scaffold/migrate.go). Reworded to 'names its source format; its target is always the next format'.

2. requirements.requirement.deck-library-upgrade's AC said upgrade 'does not read or write anything under' a deck's configured `templates:` library. The code's end-to-end validation runs the FULL `kalide start` pipeline via `validateUpgradedDeck` (template.LoadDeckLibrary honouring `templates:`, theme.LoadDir, template.NewRegistryFromLibrary, validate.Validate including deck.LoadConfig) and reads the external library read-only, exactly as `start` does, while the refresh half never opens it (internal/scaffold/upgrade.go). Reworded so the refresh step never opens the library and only the end-to-end validation reads it — read-only, no writes, no mtime changes.

3. requirements.constraint.upgrade-migrations-ordered-atomic did not state the format-bump invariant that migration idempotence rests on. Added that each real migration raises `library.yaml`'s `format:` by exactly one, and that because the chain is computed from the `format:` read once at the start of a run, a step that did not raise it would be applied again on the next run (the `formatMigration` / `migrationChain` comments, internal/scaffold/migrate.go).

4. requirements.requirement.upgrade-migrate-format and global.constraint.upgrade-unknown-format-reported described an unknown or newer format but not a chain gap. Added that a format older than `1` that no registered migration chain reaches is refused the same way — byte-for-byte untouched and reported as found vs supported — because `checkSupportedLibraryFormat` treats a missing migration-chain step as an unknown format (internal/scaffold/upgrade.go, migrate.go).

All changes [autonomous]; no judgement call was needed.
